claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Yes, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex since he's 17.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just registered with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next. He's trying to work out his options for the future.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex has registered with the careers service.

Can you tell me when exactly Alex left school? I need to know the specific date or at least the month and year when he left education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school back in the summer when term ended. So that would have been around late June or early July this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. And when did Alex register with the careers service? Was this recently, and can you tell me approximately when?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was quite recent actually - just a few weeks ago. He registered with them in early autumn, so probably around late September or early October.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to help determine Alex's eligibility.

You mentioned Alex is 17 - can you tell me his exact date of birth, or at least confirm if he has already turned 17 or when he will turn 18?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 17 earlier this year - his birthday is in March, so he's been 17 for several months now. He won't turn 18 until next March.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm a few more details:

1. Is Alex currently your responsibility - does he live with you and do you support him financially?
2. Are you (or your partner if you have one) currently responsible for Alex?

And importantly, is Alex currently in any approved education or training programme, or is he only registered with the careers service while deciding what to do next?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex lives with me and I support him - I'm his mum and he's at home with me. 

He's not in any education or training programme at the moment - he's just registered with the careers service while he figures out what he wants to do. He left school in the summer and signed up with them to get some advice about his options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying all of that information. Let me make sure I have the complete picture:

One final important question: Are you currently living in the UK, and is Alex living in the UK with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK. Alex lives here at home with me in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex left school in the summer and is not currently in education or training, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him because he registered with the careers service. 

Under UK Child Benefit rules, there's an extension period of up to **20 weeks** for young people aged 16 or 17 who have left education and register with a careers service. Since Alex only registered a few weeks ago (in late September/early October), he is still well within this 20-week extension period.

**Important things to note:**

- This extension period will eventually come to an end (20 weeks from when he registered with the careers service)
- If Alex starts an approved education or training programme before he turns 18, you may be able to continue claiming Child Benefit beyond the 20-week extension period
- Child Benefit generally stops when a young person turns 20, or earlier if they leave approved education or training (unless covered by an extension like this one)

You should apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already, and make sure to inform the Child Benefit Office of any changes to Alex's circumstances, such as if he starts education or training.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit claim?
